text: marin: dropped a quick prototype of the metrics dashboard. when window narrows legends wrap and push charts down. feels noisy. want opinions on keeping single-line legends with ellipses vs letting wrap. kevin: single-line with ellipses sounds cleaner. how do we expose full metric names? tooltip on hover + accessible label sounds good. lina: agree on ellipses. keyboard users need a way to read the full name though 6 we should avoid tooltips that aren't keyboard-triggerable. maybe make the legend items focusable and show a visible tooltip on focus. oscar: good call. also unit formatting issue: some panels auto-convert 1,234 -> 1.23K and that pushes axis tick precision. users complained about losing exactness. proposal: compact display with a persistent detail on hover/focus showing full value. marin: sample aria snippet I used in the mock: 1.23M. is role="img" ok or should we use aria-label on the number element? kevin: don't use role="img" for numeric values. put aria-label on the element itself and ensure it's announced as text. e.g., 1.23M. spelled-out numbers are friendlier to screen readers. lina: small accessibility nit: when we compress legend items, preserve a data attribute with the full metric id so screen readers can reference it. oscar: on smoothing: I like a per-chart smoothing toggle in the header. please default OFF for fidelity. we can let users pin smoothing as a dashboard-level preference later. store temporary preference in localStorage first. marin: UX question: when an outlier exceeds the y-domain we currently dim the line. that made support tickets because folks missed spikes. alternative: show a chevron overflow indicator at the top of the chart and draw the spike as a dashed extension clipped at the cap. clicking the chevron opens a panel with the real max. thoughts? e.g., [^] indicator with aria-label "value clipped: 12,345,678" kevin: love the chevron + clipped dashed line. copy for the chevron tooltip: "Value clipped at 99th percentile. Click to view full range." microcopy humility: call the action "View full range" not "Include outliers" (less ambiguous). lina: vote on copy: react :thumbsup: for "Include outliers", :thumbsup::skin-tone-2: for "View full range" (pretend reaction exists), :thinking_face: for alternatives. oscar: accessibility checklist for this feature: 1) chevron is keyboard-focusable 2) aria-label announces full value 3) panel opened by chevron includes a textual description + precise numeric values 4) legend items are reachable via keyboard. marin: implementation notes for devs: 1) cap by configurable percentile (default 99) 2) render clipped dashed extension to preserve visual cue 3) chevron/badge must have role="button" and aria-expanded toggles for the panel 4) compact units + aria-label for full value on numbers 5) smoothing toggle persisted in localStorage. kevin: perf note: rendering dashed extension for many series could be heavy. maybe only draw dashed extension for series that actually exceed the cap. keep batched draw for canvas renderer. linA: tiny copy nit in mock: change legend header from "Metrics" to "Series" 6 add a hint: "(click to inspect)" appears on hover. marin: thanks, i'll update the Figma frames. figma-bot: uploaded frame 1730000005 (dashboard-compact-legend-chevrons.png) kevin: i'll prototype keyboard tooltip behavior in the component lib. oscar can you draft aria strings for devs? oscar: yes, i'll post a short doc with examples and screen reader phrasing. expected strings: "value clipped: twelve million three hundred forty five thousand six hundred seventy eight", "legend: request latency p50" etc. marin: action items: 1) design: single-line ellipsis legend + focusable tooltip 2) design: chevron overflow + dashed clip + panel 3) dev: aria-label on compact numbers with spelled-out values 4) dev: smoothing toggle default OFF, localStorage persist 5) copy: use "View full range" for chevron action. kevin: i'll pick up #3 and start a sketch for keyboard tooltips. marin: thanks all 6 I'll push updated frames by tomorrow morning.
